EmbeddingsGemini Embedding 2Extract text from documents and create production embeddings (OCR + retrieval).$0.10 / 1M tokens
Embed fallbackHuggingFace all-MiniLMFallback embeddings for POC and offline or cost-sensitive use.self-hosted (~free)
GenerationDeepSeek V4 FlashGenerate grounded answers, explanations, quizzes, activities and assessments with citations.₹0.14 / query
VerificationQwen 3.6 Flash — JudgeJudge groundedness, relevance, pedagogy and bias safety for the policy gate. Deliberately a different provider than the DeepSeek generator, so the judge isn't grading its own family's output.≈₹0.0154 / verification — ~half DeepSeek's rate
Image · primaryGPT Image 2 LowGenerate high-quality, text-aware images for explanations and visuals.₹0.578 / image
Image · fallbackQwen-Image-2512Fallback image generation, triggered only when the primary model fails or times out.$0.02 / image (API)
Voice-to-text · demoGroq Whisper large-v3-turboTranscribe mic-button voice input to text — single synchronous API call, near-instant response.free tier → ~$0.04/hr audio, paid tier
Voice-to-text · productionAmazon Transcribe StreamingCloud STT replacing Groq, matched to today's instant mic-button feel via a persistent WebSocket audio stream instead of one-shot upload. Requires a client-side rewrite before launch — not a config swap. Same AWS account as storage/hosting/Polly.$0.024/min (base tier), 15s minimum billed per request
Text-to-voice · demoOn-device TTS (macOS say + ffmpeg)Narrate generated content for offline playback, female / male voices.~free (local, macOS-only)
Text-to-voice · productionAmazon Polly — Neural voicesCloud narration replacing macOS say, which cannot run on the Linux AWS hosting in this stack. Same AWS account as storage/hosting — no new vendor.$16 / 1M characters
Why TTS needs to change for production: the demo's narration engine shells out to macOS's built-in say command plus ffmpeg — it only exists on macOS. The AWS hosting tier documented in this file runs Linux (EC2/ECS), where say does not exist, so text-to-voice will silently fail in production unless it's swapped for a cloud TTS API before launch.
Why STT also changes for production: Groq Whisper works fine as a demo dependency, but launch moves it to Amazon Transcribe Streaming for AWS account consolidation. Unlike the TTS swap, this isn't a drop-in replacement — Groq's endpoint is a single synchronous upload-and-transcribe call, while matching that same instant mic-button feel on Transcribe requires the client to open a persistent streaming connection and send continuous audio chunks. Budget real front-end engineering time for this before launch, not just a backend config change. Transcribe's standard batch API is simpler to integrate but adds several seconds of lag per question — avoid it for this use case.

Demo and production are intentionally different

what runs today vs. what ships

The demo optimizes for zero or minimal provider cost. Production optimizes for predictable quality, text-bearing educational visuals, document grounding and measurable validation — with every AI model called by API, no self-hosted GPU inference to operate.

CURRENT DEMO

Free / low-cost provider chain

  • Flask + Jinja2 + SQLAlchemy application
  • DeepSeek → Gemini 1.5 Flash → Groq → local FLAN-T5 fallback for text — DeepSeek/Gemini keys are not currently set; live demo traffic runs entirely on the Groq step (Llama 3.3 70B, free tier)
  • BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 + LlamaIndex hybrid vector/keyword retrieval
  • Cloudflare FLUX.1 Schnell → Pollinations → RunPod image fallback
  • S3 image cache, Razorpay checkout, AWS/Cloudflare delivery
  • Voice-to-text: Groq-hosted Whisper large-v3-turbo API (mic button, free tier, same key pool as text)
  • Text-to-voice: macOS say command + ffmpeg — on-device narration, cached to MP3 by content hash, zero cost, macOS-only (won't run on Linux hosting)
  • Explicit unlimited teacher/student demo accounts for frictionless demonstrations

Purpose: product demonstration and workflow validation. These free-provider costs are not used in the production margin table.

APPROVED PRODUCTION

Governed education AI stack

  • Gemini Embedding 2 for OCR + production embeddings
  • OpenAI text-embedding-3-small API for embeddings fallback — cheapest option, no self-hosting
  • DeepSeek V4 Flash for user-facing answer generation; Qwen 3.6 Flash for independent answer verification — a genuinely different provider from the generator, at a comparable cheap-tier price, no self-hosting
  • GPT Image 2 Low primary; Qwen-Image-2512 fallback via Replicate/WaveSpeed API — cheapest at $0.02/image, no self-hosting
  • Voice-to-text: Amazon Transcribe Streaming replaces Groq Whisper — same AWS account as storage/Polly, but needs a real client-side rewrite (WebSocket audio streaming) to keep today's instant response feel; $0.024/min base tier, 15s minimum per request
  • Text-to-voice: Amazon Polly (Neural) replaces the macOS-only say engine, which cannot run on Linux hosting — $16/1M characters, same AWS account
  • Policy gates, audit and tenant isolation
  • Application tier hosted on AWS (EC2/RDS/S3/CloudFront) — see AWS Hosting Cost tab

Purpose: commercial delivery using the model and control layers shown in the Architecture tab. Launch stack is API-only for every AI model; self-hosted GPU inference is a later scale option, not a launch requirement.

Configuration issue to close before production: the demo provider chain still defaults to legacy aliases such as deepseek-chat and gemini-1.5-flash. The paid environment must set and test explicit production model identifiers rather than relying on demo defaults.

every layer, every responsibility
LayerComponentsResponsibility
Client & experienceTeacher web app, student web app, responsive UICreate, curate, learn, assess, chat, documents, visuals and audio.
Application & orchestrationFlask 3.1 blueprints, Flask-Login/RBAC, deterministic task router, personalization engine, Markdown/Mermaid/infographic/story renderersSecure request handling and controlled AI workflows.
VoiceGroq Whisper large-v3-turbo (speech-to-text, demo only) · Amazon Transcribe Streaming (speech-to-text, production) · macOS say+ffmpeg (text-to-speech, demo only) · Amazon Polly Neural (text-to-speech, production)Mic-button transcription and narration playback; both STT and TTS engines swap at launch — STT for AWS account consolidation (with a required client-side streaming rewrite), TTS because the demo engine is macOS-only and cannot run on Linux hosting.
Document ingestionValidation, PDF/DOCX/TXT extraction, checksum/versioning, PII redaction, chunks and metadata, Gemini Embedding 2 (text-embedding-3-small API fallback)Produce governed, attributable and searchable source material.
Personalized RAGInjection check, query optimization, tenant/document filters, 70/30 hybrid retrieval, learner context, DeepSeek V4 FlashGenerate source-grounded answers with citations.
VerificationAtomic claim extraction, keyword evidence matching, Qwen 3.6 Flash judge (API, different provider from the generator) and policy gatePASS returns; RETRY corrects unsupported claims; ESCALATE routes to human review.
Data, audit & operationsSQLAlchemy + SQLite, LlamaIndex VectorStore, file storage, audit/verification logs, environment-based secretsMVP persistence and traceability. PostgreSQL/pgvector remains the scale-up path.
Model stackGemini Embedding 2 (text-embedding-3-small API fallback), DeepSeek V4 Flash (generation), Qwen 3.6 Flash (independent judge), GPT Image 2 Low, Qwen-Image-2512 API fallback, Amazon Transcribe Streaming (STT), Amazon Polly Neural (TTS)OCR/embeddings, answer generation, independent cross-provider verification, resilient text-aware images and speech — all API-based, no GPU to host.
Application hostingAWS: EC2/ECS app servers, RDS PostgreSQL, S3, CloudFront, ALBRuns the Flask application tier and serves cached assets; carries no AI model compute — see AWS Hosting Cost tab.
Cross-cutting controlsPII protection, injection defense, tenant isolation, RBAC, source approval, versioning, bounded retry and telemetrySafety, governance and operational control across every pipeline.
Model separation: DeepSeek V4 Flash writes the user-facing answer, and a Qwen 3.6 Flash call from a different provider independently judges the candidate and evidence — this replaces an earlier design where DeepSeek judged its own answer, which risked a model grading its own output favorably. Both are API calls, so launch requires no GPU to provision or operate. Self-hosting a dedicated judge is a later option for scale, privacy or data-residency needs, not a launch dependency.

Full-quota unit economics

same sequence as the architecture request path

Customer prices and quotas remain unchanged. Every included quota is assumed consumed. The launch-cost baseline uses DeepSeek V4 Flash for answer generation at ₹0.14/query and Qwen 3.6 Flash (a different provider, judging independently) for verification at ≈₹0.0154/call — sourced from Alibaba's official qwen-flash pricing ($0.05/1M input + $0.40/1M output, International/Singapore tier) applied to a typical ~2,000-input/150-output-token judge call — plus GPT Image 2 Low at the approved ₹0.578/image planning rate.

Judge cost update: these are contribution margins, not accounting net margins. The ≈₹0.0154 verification rate is sourced directly from Alibaba Cloud's official qwen-flash pricing page (International/Singapore tier: $0.05/1M input tokens, $0.40/1M output tokens, 0–256K context), applied to a typical judge call's token count — roughly half of DeepSeek V4 Flash's ₹0.03/call, not the "similar price" originally assumed. Alibaba's Mainland-China endpoint prices ~60–70% lower still, and a 50% batch-call discount is available on both endpoints if judge calls can be queued rather than run real-time — neither is modeled here. Both DeepSeek and Qwen invoice by actual input/output token volume, so real judge cost must still be logged and reconciled against this estimate. GST, payment fees, refunds, support, salaries, monitoring, backups and bad debt remain excluded.

Qwen fallback cost guardrail

Base margins assume GPT Image 2 serves normal traffic. Using the Replicate/WaveSpeed managed-API rate of $0.02/image and the approved ₹96.35/USD planning FX gives approximately ₹1.927/Qwen image, or ₹1.349 more than the ₹0.578 GPT planning rate.

Operating rule: alert when Qwen-Image exceeds 1% of monthly visual requests. A sustained 10% fallback rate breaks the 50% Pro margin floor in the high-infrastructure case.

Reading this table: the Lean, Single-AZ configuration is the right launch choice — at 750+ paying subscribers it already lands inside the approved ₹7.90–₹21/user range. Move to Production/HA only once subscriber count and uptime commitments justify roughly 4× the fixed AWS spend.
Not included: data-transfer spikes beyond assumed egress, WAF/Shield, secrets manager, CI/CD, staging environment, cross-region backup replication, and reserved-instance/Savings-Plan discounts (typically 30–45% cheaper for 1-year committed compute and RDS).

Defensible message

"Turn your own curriculum into grounded explanations, visual analogies, quizzes, activities and graded assessments." That bundle is more defensible than claiming only document Q&A or AI summaries.

Primary pressure

NotebookLM already offers generous free document chat and study artifacts. Askoodle must demonstrate better classroom workflow, consistent text inside visuals, rubric-based validation and India-specific usability.
